Hi, I'm Tom, and I'm a recruiter in Miami. I find people for companies in the United States and in Latin America. Last year I worked on a job for an HR director in Brazil. The posting asked for fluent English. We got about two hundred applications, but many of the best people didn't apply. I called some of them later. They all said the same thing: I didn't think my English was good enough. In the end, we hired a woman with very good experience and clear, simple English. Her English was not perfect, and that was not a problem. So my advice is: read the requirements, but don't give up before the deadline.

My name is Sophie. Three years ago I saw a job in Edinburgh, in Scotland. It was my dream job, but it asked for experience with international teams, and I didn't have much. I wrote my application on a Sunday, and then I didn't send it. On Monday I read it again. On Tuesday, the last day, I sent it at eleven at night, one hour before the deadline. A week later, a recruiter called me. I was so nervous that I forgot my own phone number! I didn't get that job. But the recruiter remembered me, and two months later she offered me a better one.
